## Summary

Measure whether the child-port discovery fix (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF, deployed
2026-10-26T21:01Z) actually eliminates router-responder `GET /slots ... 500`
responses over a full 24 h production window, and record the raw counts as
auditable evidence.

**Earliest run: 2026-10-27T12:00Z.** Window:
**2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z.** If the fix (or a follow-up restart)
lands later than that, shift the window to start 24 h after the last relevant
deployment and record the new timestamps in a comment.

**Window state verified at planning (2026-10-28T04:40Z):** the window is
**still open** (≈7 h 20 m remaining at verification time). Production facts:
proxy pid **3791954** started **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** and is still running
(18 h 23 m uptime) — the fixed proxy has been up continuously since **before**
the window opened, and **no proxy restart has occurred inside the window**, so
the AC6 restart condition is satisfiable. No pre-window baseline comment was
recorded at 12:00Z; see "Baseline reconstruction" under the execute-time plan
for why the counter delta is nonetheless provable.

## Problem statement

Router-proxied `GET /slots` polls returned HTTP 500 at ~9 % during giant
prefills because child-port discovery silently failed and every proxy poll
traversed the router. The fix replaced discovery with a rotation-proof signal
and routed every call site through it, but the only proof that matters is a
production 24 h window with zero such 500s — the pre-fix evidence (1,754
router 500s in the 2026-10-26 log) is not proof of absence.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainer** — "As the operator, I want a dated, reproducible
  measurement of router-responder `/slots` 500s so I can close the residual-500
  bug and trust the fix, instead of re-reading raw logs myself."
- **On-call agent (herdr downtime worker)** — "As an unattended agent, I want a
  deterministic method and explicit verdict rule so my pass/fail report does
  not depend on my own judgement of ambiguous counts."
- **Downstream users** — chat/agent clients that see 500s and 5–7 s slot-poll
  latency when slot queries serialise behind a busy child.

## Acceptance Criteria

Refined at intake per producer decisions Q1(a), Q2(b), Q3(a):

- **AC1** — **Chat-model path: zero.** The windowed count of router-responder
  `GET /slots ... 500` responses attributable to the chat model is **0**.
  Responder split: lines with no `[pid]` prefix are the router, `[pid]`-prefixed
  lines are the model children; per-file counts are reported for every
  `llama-server*.log` file whose mtime falls inside the window (Q1a).
- **AC2** — **Raw router and child counts reported**, so a silent switch back to
  router polling cannot masquerade as a pass: router-responder `GET /slots`
  200 / 400 / 500 and model-child 200 / 400 / 500 counts for each file in the
  window. `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` output is attached verbatim.
- **AC3** — **`slots_stale` share reported** for `status_request` polls in the
  window: the primary figure is *all* `status_request` polls (directly
  comparable to the pre-fix baseline **579/899** in the 2026-10-26 file), with
  the active-prefill subset (`active_query=true` or `local_active_query=true`)
  reported as a secondary figure (Q3a).
- **AC4** — **Fallback evidence reported, split by path** (Q2b):
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  delta across the window plus the (throttled, undercounting)
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning lines, attributed by model.
  - Chat-model (`Qwen3`) fallbacks: **any occurrence fails the check.**
  - Embed-model (`mxbai-embed`) fallbacks: reported separately as a
    **non-blocking observation**; if any occur, a new bug item is filed at
    window end, linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`.
- **AC5** — **Reproducibility:** the exact commands/regexes (or script
  invocations) used, the window start/end timestamps, the pre-window baseline
  snapshot (counter values, log line count, proxy pid + start time) and the raw
  counts are all recorded as a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — **Restart integrity:** any proxy restart inside the window is
  detected (pid change) and reported; if one occurred, the counter delta is
  declared unavailable and the verdict relies on per-file log counts with the
  limitation stated explicitly.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Method (agreed: Q1 option (a) — hybrid)

Measured with existing tooling plus two log families:

```bash
# 1. Window-start snapshot (also record: date -u, pid start time, log line count)
date -u; ps -o lstart= -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app')"
wc -l < /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'

# 2. Window-end snapshot (same commands, 24 h later) -> counter delta = exact
#    windowed fallbacks when the proxy was not restarted in between.

# 3. Responder/status split per file (reuses the triage CLI: no timestamps in
#    llama-server logs, so scope by the files whose mtime falls in the window)
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary

# 4. Fallback warnings (throttled to one line per interval -> undercounts;
#    the counter above is authoritative)
grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log

# slots_stale share (existing baseline method)
grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | sort | uniq -c
```

Take a **pre-window baseline snapshot** immediately before
2026-10-27T12:00Z (counter values + `llama-server.log` line count + proxy pid
start time) so the window delta is unambiguous.

> **Status: not done.** No snapshot comment exists for 2026-10-27T12:00Z. The
execution plan below reconstructs the baseline from monotonic-counter
evolution plus pid `lstart`, and states the limitation explicitly (AC5).

## Execution plan (exact recipe — run at/after 2026-10-28T12:00Z)

Steps 0–2 must be re-verified at run time, not trusted from this block; they
are read-only and cheap. Steps 3–6 produce the evidence; step 7 records it.

### Step 0 — window gate

Do **not** measure before **2026-10-28T12:00Z**. An earlier run measures a
partial window and is not acceptable as the AC evidence.

### Step 1 — restart integrity (AC6)

```bash
date -u
ps -o pid,lstart,etime -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app' | head -1)"
```

Expected: a single pid **3791954** with `lstart` **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** ⇒ no
restart inside the window. Any other pid/`lstart` ⇒ record the restart time,
declare the counter delta unavailable, and fall back to per-file log counts
with the limitation stated (AC6).

### Step 2 — fallback counter (AC4, exact)

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'
```

A Prometheus counter that has never been incremented emits **no sample line**
(only `# HELP` / `# TYPE`). That is the state observed at planning — quote the
raw output verbatim, because "absent sample" is the auditable form of "0".
Range-vector deltas are not needed: a monotonic counter reading 0 on a process
that started before the window ⇒ windowed delta = 0.

### Baseline reconstruction (AC5, replaces the missed 12:00Z snapshot)

State the limitation explicitly and rebuild the baseline from: proxy pid +
`lstart` (step 1); the counter's never-incremented state (step 2); the per-file
line counts read at window end. The proof is monotonicity, not a start sample:
the process started 1 h 44 m before the window opened and its counter is still
0.

### Step 3 — llama-server file set (AC1 / AC2)

```bash
ls -l --time-style=full-iso /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server*.log*
```

Window set (mtime inside 2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z):
`llama-server.log-2026-10-28` (logrotate `copytruncate` copy at 00:00Z; content
= 2026-10-27T00:00Z → 2026-10-28T00:00Z) and the live `llama-server.log`
(content = 2026-10-28T00:00Z → window end). `llama-server.log-2026-10-27.gz`
has mtime 2026-10-27T00:00Z ⇒ outside the window, exclude it.

llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**, so this union covers
2026-10-27T00:00Z → window end: a **superset** of the window, carrying 12 h of
extra pre-window traffic. Consequence: **zero router-responder 500s across the
superset proves zero inside the window** (report the over-count direction); a
non-zero count needs the per-file split plus the caveat that the window
boundary is approximate at ±12 h granularity.

```bash
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --llama-file 'llama-server.log-2026-10-28' --summary
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary
```

Record both per-file outputs verbatim (AC2) and sum the responder/status matrix
(router 200/400/500, child 200/400/500).

### Step 4 — proxy.log file set (AC3, plus AC4 warnings)

`proxy.log` is timestamped and self-rotates every 6 h, and the daily
`copytruncate` copy (`proxy.log-YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) can duplicate a range — so
**file names do not reliably delimit the window**. Derive each candidate's own
first/last timestamp from its lines, keep the parts intersecting the window,
and dedupe overlapping ranges (keep one generation per timestamp range):

```bash
for f in /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*; do
  case "$f" in *.gz) zcat "$f";; *) cat "$f";; esac \
    | awk -v f="$f" 'NR==1{first=$0} {last=$0} END{print f"	"substr(first,1,19)"	"substr(last,1,19)}'
done
```

At planning time the window-relevant generations were
`proxy.log.2026-10-27_10`, `proxy.log.2026-10-27_16`, `proxy.log.2026-10-27_22`,
`proxy.log-2026-10-28_00` and the live `proxy.log` — indicative only; re-derive
the set from timestamps at run time.

```bash
# AC3 primary: all status_request polls in the window (comparable to 579/899)
grep -h 'status_request' <window files> | grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
# AC3 secondary: active-prefill subset
grep -h 'status_request' <window files> \
  | grep -o 'active_query=[a-z]*\|local_active_query=[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
# AC4 warnings, per file (throttled -> undercounts; the step-2 counter is authoritative)
for f in <window files>; do printf '%s	' "$f"; grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' "$f"; done
grep -h 'slots_child_port_unavailable' <window files>   # attribute each by model=
```

### Step 5 — verdict rule

**GREEN** ⇔ chat-model router-responder `/slots` 500s = 0 **and** chat-model
fallback delta = 0 (counter **and** warning lines). Embed-model
(`mxbai-embed`) occurrences are reported separately and file a linked bug
(`discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`) without ever making the verdict RED.
Any other positive chat-model count ⇒ **RED**: name the model/responder and
file the linked bug. Report router/child 200/400 counts and the `slots_stale`
share alongside either way (AC2/AC3).

### Step 6 — evidence comment (AC5)

One comment recording: window start/end; `date -u` at run time; pid + `lstart`
+ uptime; the raw `/metrics` line(s); both per-file triage outputs verbatim;
the `proxy.log` file set with each file's observed first/last timestamp; the
dedupe/overlap rule applied; the counts; the `slots_stale` primary and
active-prefill figures; the "llama-server lines are timestamp-free ⇒ ±12 h
boundary approximation" caveat; the missed-baseline limitation; the verdict;
and any linked bug id.

AC7 and AC8 are code-change boilerplate on a measurement item — see the OPEN
QUESTION in the Appendix for the interpretation used.

## Existing state (evidence gathered at intake, 2026-10-26T23:36Z)

- **Fix is deployed.** Proxy pid 3482545 restarted 2026-10-26T21:01:42Z
  (after fix commits `f58e8964` 2026-10-26T12:51Z and `189864fc`
  2026-10-26T13:00Z, both on `dev`). Blocking item LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF is
  `completed`/`in_review`. _(Superseded 2026-10-27T10:16:11Z: pid 3482545 was
  replaced by pid **3791954**, still running at planning time. Both fix commits
  are ancestors of `dev`. The restart predates the window, so the window is
  restart-free.)_
- **Early signal the chat path is fixed.** Live 90 s spot check at
  23:36Z: 78 model-responder `/slots` events, **0** router-responder `/slots`
  events, 0 HTTP 500s.
- **Residual fallbacks exist post-fix.** `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  is already **4** since the 21:01:42Z restart, and one throttled
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING was logged at **21:01:46Z** for
  `model=mxbai-embed` (the embedding child). The current `llama-server.log`
  also still holds ~4 router-responder `/slots` lines in its last ~25 min.
  Consequence: AC4's "one occurrence fails" will very likely trip on
  restart/embed transients — resolved as Q2 option (b).
- **Rotation breaks the single-file method.** `llama-server.log` is rotated
  in-process (`rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)`, numeric `llama-server.N.log`) and
  by the `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` safety net (daily, `copytruncate`,
  `dateext` → `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD`). `proxy.log` self-rotates every
  6 h (`proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH`). A 24 h window therefore spans several
  files, and llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**
  (`scripts/slots_500_triage.py` documents this: "no timestamps in
  llama-server logs; the corpus is per-file"). A single-file grep cannot
  cover the window — resolved at intake as Q1 option (a), hybrid.
- **Cumulative figures today** (`--llama-file 'llama-server.log'`, whole
  file, spans more than one day and predates the fixed restart):
  router 200 = 38,369; router 400 = 452; router 500 = 2,753; model 200 /
  child 200 = 68,610 + 8. Non-zero router 200s show that **direct LAN clients
  poll the router** legitimately, so raw router counts are not pure
  proxy-fallback evidence.
- **`slots_stale` alive in the current `proxy.log`**: 2,019 false / 1,952 true
  (49 % true) since the current file began — usable as an intermediate
  reference, not the window figure.
- **No existing windowed tool.** `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` classifies by
  responder/status and supports `--llama-file <glob>`, but has no
  `--since/--until`; window scoping is a manual file-set decision.

## Desired change

No product code change: this item is a **measurement and evidence** task. Its
"change" is a recorded, reproducible verdict (counts, commands, window
timestamps, and either a green pass or a new linked bug when red).

**Verdict rule (agreed):** GREEN = windowed chat-model router-responder
`/slots` 500s are 0 **and** the chat-model fallback delta is 0, with router and
child 200/400 counts and the `slots_stale` share reported alongside. RED = any
positive chat-model count; a RED verdict must name the model/responder and
create a linked bug item (`discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`). Embed-model
fallbacks never make the verdict RED — they raise a linked bug instead.

## Constraints

- Window must be a full 24 h with the fixed proxy running; restarts inside the
  window must be detected and reported (they reset counters).
- No production restart, no config change, and no code change is needed for the
  measurement itself (`start-proxy` must not be invoked unless the proxy dies).
- llama-server logs are timestamp-free → any time attribution is per-file and
  approximate; this limitation must be stated in the recorded comment, never
  silently smoothed over.
- If the verdict is red, a new bug item is created (linked
  `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`); LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF is never silently
  reopened.

data.description:
# Intake Brief — In-request local re-dispatch after a prefill-deadline cancellation re-arms the lease and holds the gate ~6 min

## Problem statement

A local dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` (120 s) does not reliably
end the session's claim on the local gate: the same session immediately re-dispatches
local and acquires a **fresh dispatch lease**, whose record stays `active` without
producing a first byte and is released only by the no-progress watchdog ~308 s later.
Other sessions are denied (`local_dispatch_denied`, `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue
reason=local_lease_active`) for 311–322 s each — beyond the epic's <=5 min per-hold bound
(LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6 AC1) and the only remaining `wedge_denials > 0` signal
(`ac1.wedge_denials: 3` in the 2026-10-25 21:19 → 2026-10-26 21:19 window, verified
`ac1.verdict_met: false`).

## Users / stakeholders

- **Operator** (user story): *"As an operator, I want a local dispatch cancelled by the
  prefill deadline to stop holding the local dispatch gate, so the next session is not
  denied for longer than the epic's <=5 min bound."*
- **Sessions sharing the local gateway**: during the hold they are forced remote
  (3 refusals in this incident, 311–322 s each; the 2026-10-23 incident was ~3 orders
  of magnitude larger and unbounded).

## Mechanism decision (intake determination, 2026-10-26 — log `proxy.log.2026-10-26_131429`)

**Candidate (a) is confirmed; candidate (b) is refuted as the operative mechanism:**

1. `[local] POST` fires **147–150 ms after** each `lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`
   (10:39:36,396 → 10:39:36,546; 10:41:36,629 → 10:41:36,776) — a fresh local dispatch
   in the same request/retry window, so a *new* record is acquired **after** the release.
2. `_extend_lease_during_prefill` only mutates an **existing active** record, yet
   `lease_extended_during_prefill ... in_flight=True` resumes at 10:41:46, exactly 10 s
   after the 10:41:36 release — proving a fresh **active** record exists post-release
   (mechanism (b) — release removing a differently-keyed record — would leave no record
   for the extension path to touch; the release path only logs `lease_released` when it
   actually removed a record).
3. The hold chain: record acquired ~10:44:25 (same session re-acquisition — always
   permitted by `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`): no extensions after 10:44:18, denials at
   10:46:57/10:47:08 with `owner=01a177c6…`, released 10:47:33 by
   `reason=no_progress_watchdog` (≈10:44:25 + 180 s watchdog + 10 s sweep) ≈ **308 s
   unproductive hold** → AC3's 300 s bound fails.
4. **Residual gap (OPEN at implementation time):** the thrash cooldown was armed for this
   session at 10:39:36 and re-armed at 10:41:36 (`prefill_thrash_cooldown_started cooldown_s=600`),
   yet **zero** `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` lines appear for
   `01a177c6-…` in the whole file across 4 successive local dispatches (10:39:36 → 10:44:25),
   while `herdr-…` sessions are consistently skipped. The
   `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining(_session_id, …)` gate in `provider.py` returned 0 for
   this session despite the armed key. Either the arm key differs from the check key
   (session-identity mismatch between router.py's arm and provider.py's check), or a
   dispatch path bypasses the local-branch gate — the AC1 deterministic test must pin this
   before choosing the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` is **not re-dispatched locally
   within the same request** (the detour goes to the next provider), **or** the
   re-dispatch is refused while the session's prefill-thrash cooldown is active — and the
   gate actually engages: asserted by a deterministic test with an injected clock and a
   stubbed local dispatcher (mirroring `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`) that
   would have caught this incident (i.e. it fails on the pre-fix behaviour of a fresh
   lease acquired 150 ms after the release). The test must also isolate why the
   2026-10-26 gate did not engage (arm-key vs check-key or bypass path) and assert the
   engaged skip.
2. After the cancellation the session's lease **and** `local_prefill_in_flight` marker are
   cleared before any retry, and the cancelled upstream prefill is cancelled (or proven
   dead) so `_extend_prefill_lease` cannot re-extend from a stale marker.
3. Any hold that does remain is bounded by <=300 s (the epic's 5 min bound): a regression
   test asserts release within 300 s simulated (no-progress watchdog must bound the record
   even when the session re-acquires).
4. `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure` over a >=24 h post-fix window
   reports `ac1.wedge_denials: 0` with no 300 s+ unproductive hold chain and
   `ac1.verdict_met: true`.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments,
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md`, and the prefill-recovery verification
   doc/README as applicable).
6. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The prefill deadline (120 s / 90 s default) is a deliberate
  "detour, don't kill" backstop; the fix must not push first-byte latency above
  `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds` and must not disable the thrash cooldown
  (`local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds`, rollback knob 0).
- The no-progress watchdog (180 s) and 10 s cleanup sweep cadence are production-bounded
  self-healing; the <=300 s bound must hold without weakening them.
- No-preemption lease semantics (same-session re-acquisition permitted) are load-bearing for
  legitimate long prefills; the fix must not break admission for genuine in-flight prefills.
- Fix scope lives in this item (the epic closes with this residual tracked; see Related work).

## Existing state

- `router.py`: on `prefill_deadline_exceeded` it arms the 600 s thrash cooldown, releases
  the lease + marker (`_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`), then the chain falls through —
  but the *next* local attempt (same request re-dispatch/retry) acquires a fresh lease;
  the thrash gate in `provider.py` did not engage for the affected session (see mechanism
  decision §4).
- `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` counts `active or expires_at > now` records as occupied;
  the sweep only deletes `not active AND expired` records outright, and the active-expired
  category extends records whose llama-server slot still reports processing — a wedged
  record can hold the pool until the no-progress watchdog.

## Desired change

- The post-deadline detour must be **terminal for local within that request** (no in-request
  local re-dispatch), and/or the thrash-cooldown gate must demonstrably engage for every
  local dispatch attempt (close the arm-key/check-key or bypass-path gap).
- Every local dispatch record must be released (or bounded) within <=300 s of its last
  progress, regardless of which path acquired it (deadline detour, same-session
  re-acquisition, active-expired sweep).
- `local_prefill_in_flight` must never outlive the dispatch it marks (no stale marker
  re-extension).

## Risks, assumptions and failure modes

- **Assumption:** the deployed llama-server's first byte genuinely arrives with the SSE
  headers (the monitor's premise), so a 120 s deadline miss means no client-visible byte —
  supported by 0 `Stream started: provider=local` lines for the session in the window.
- **Risk — over-correction:** making the deadline detour terminal for local could deny
  local to a session whose next *legitimate* request would have prefilled warm; mitigated by
  the existing 600 s cooldown already having this intent, and by clearing the cooldown on a
  successful local first byte.
- **Risk — masking the gate gap:** capping renewals only (the LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0 shape)
  bounds the hold but leaves the un-engaged thrash gate; AC1 must assert the gate engages.
- **Failure mode to test:** stale `local_prefill_in_flight` marker re-extending a record
  whose upstream is dead (`in_flight=True` extensions resumed after the release).
- **Scope-creep risk:** lease fairness (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0) and the 115 s second-slot
  residual (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) overlap this evidence; record any such work as linked
  items, do not absorb it here.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — local re-dispatch / slot-retry path after a deadline
  cancellation; thrash-cooldown routing gate (`_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining`),
  `_dispatch_local` call sites
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — deadline arm/release sequence
  (`prefill_deadline_exceeded`, `_record_prefill_thrash_cooldown`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`), `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` caller
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_extend_lease_during_prefill`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch`, `_watchdog_no_progress`,
  `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_*`, `_dispatch_lease_key`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` — deterministic injected-clock/stub harness
  to extend for the re-dispatch assertion
- `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` — AC4 measurement (`ac1.wedge_denials`,
  hold-chain accounting in `measure_wedge_denials`)

## Related work

- **LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6** — epic "Wedged prefill lease loop holds the local dispatch gate
  ~4 h" (completed/in_review); epic AC1 is the <=5 min bound this item enforces. The
  producer removed the epic's `depends-on` edge so the epic can advance: the epic closes
  with this residual tracked here (blocking edges on this item: none).
- **LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0** — Lease fairness (cap consecutive prefill-lease renewals); same
  log evidence; producer decided the epic closes with this residual tracked here, and the
  fix *may* land there instead only if the cooldown/lease cap also covers the in-request
  re-dispatch (AC1 allows either mechanism; otherwise fix here and note the overlap).
- **LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I** — 115 s/24 h second-slot residual (separate admission-shape
  residual; not to be conflated).
- **LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI** — Contention queue ignores prefill-saturated dispatches
  (completed; related queue behaviour).
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** — Stale local dispatch lease blocks subsequent requests
  (completed; prior stale-lease fix lineage).
- **LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2** — AC3 re-judgement that surfaced this residual
  (24 h window 2026-10-25 21:19 → 2026-10-26 21:19).

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q (producer, via description): "Which mechanism holds the gate — (a) the same request's
  local re-dispatch acquiring a fresh record, or (b) a differently-keyed release?"
  — Answer (intake, from log `proxy.log.2026-10-26_131429` + code read): **(a)** confirmed;
  (b) refuted (see Mechanism decision). Source: `[local] POST` 147–150 ms after each
  `lease_released`; `lease_extended_during_prefill in_flight=True` resuming 10 s after the
  release proves a fresh active record (the extension path only mutates an existing active
  record); watchdog release at 10:47:33 = 10:44:25 acquisition + 180 s + 10 s sweep.
- Q (implement comment): "the release line carries `endpoint=http://localhost:8080`, the
  extension path passes its own endpoint argument — is endpoint-key normalisation the
  defect?" — Answer (intake): no. `_dispatch_lease_key` does **not** normalise
  (`localhost:8080` vs `192.168.0.199:8000` are distinct keys), but the 10:41:46 post-release
  extension proves a live record under the extension path's key, and the release path only
  logs `lease_released` when it removed a record — so the record that wedged was acquired
  after the release, not left behind by a wrong-key release. The endpoint mismatch on the
  release line remains worth a defensive check (key-form consistency) at implementation time.
- Q (OPEN QUESTION — implementation must answer before choosing the fix): why did the
  600 s thrash cooldown armed at 10:39:36/10:41:36 for `01a177c6-…` fail to produce a
  single `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` across 4 successive local
  dispatches (10:39:36 → 10:44:25), while `herdr-…` sessions were consistently skipped?
  — Answer: **_not yet determined_**. Hypotheses to test with the AC1 injected-clock harness:
  (i) session-id mismatch between router.py's arm key (`session.session_id`) and
  provider.py's check key (`_session_id`, raw `x-session-id`/`session_id` header); or
  (ii) a local dispatch path that bypasses provider.py's local-branch gate.
  **Recommended (advisory):** treat the gate engagement as load-bearing — assert it in the
  deterministic test and fix whichever arm/check or bypass gap the test surfaces, rather
  than only capping renewals (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0-style), so AC1 holds for any path.
  Idempotence note: re-running intake must not duplicate this appendix entry.
data.title: In-request local re-dispatch after a prefill-deadline cancellation re-arms the lease and holds the gate ~6 min (3 wedge denials, 2026-10-26 10:41-10:47)

data.description:
**Headline:** Re-arm the proxy's existing (currently disabled) session-compaction machinery at the local→remote boundary: when a session that has been served locally is about to be dispatched to a remote provider, summarise its oldest turns on the session's **own** local slot, release that slot immediately, and send the small compacted history upstream.

**Status:** plan complete — the three design decisions were confirmed by the producer (Appendix Q1–Q3) and are reflected in the ACs below; the work is decomposed into 7 dependency-ordered child items (see the Planning Complete comment).

## Problem statement

A session that starts on the local model and later moves to a remote provider carries its full grown history to the remote LLM, paying for the whole context as new input tokens even though most of it has already been worked through locally. The proxy already has a complete summarisation/compaction implementation (`proxy/proxy/compaction.py`, `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`, `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`), but it is only evaluated at prompt-assembly/oversized-bypass time and is globally disabled in config (`server.compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`). We want that machinery re-armed at the *local→remote boundary*: when a request for an already-locally-served session is about to be dispatched remote, summarise the oldest turns using the session's **own** local slot (whose KV is disposable at that moment) and send the small compacted history upstream.

## Users

- **Agent operator** (primary): long audit/implement sessions start local and escalate remote; wants remote spend and remote prompt size cut without losing the thread of work.
- **Local model capacity** (secondary): the slot already assigned to the session is released as soon as the summary is produced, so local capacity is not held while the remote stream runs.
- **Proxy maintainer**: wants one obvious, gated, fail-open hook rather than another parallel compaction path.

Example user stories:

- As the operator, when a long session that has been served locally falls back to a remote provider, I want the remote prompt compacted so the first remote turn does not cost ~200K input tokens.
- As the operator, I want the summarisation to use the slot my session already owns (not another session's warm slot), and for that slot to be free again the moment summarisation finishes.
- As a maintainer, when the summariser fails, times out, or returns an empty summary, I want the request to go remote with its history untouched and a structured log line recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Boundary trigger.** When a request for a session with **at least one prior locally-served turn recorded in the session store** (the agreed provenance signal — Appendix Q1) is about to be dispatched to a `type: remote` provider, the proxy evaluates boundary compaction *before* the remote request is sent, and dispatches the compacted message list upstream when compaction succeeds. Provenance must not be derived from a live slot assignment (a released or save/restored slot must not disqualify the session). A session with no prior local service (remote-only model, or local never used) and a session below the agreed minimum-size guard are unchanged.
- **AC2 — Slot reuse.** The summarisation call is pinned to the local llama-server slot currently assigned to that session (`id_slot` from the session→slot registry), so it reuses the session's own disposable slot instead of taking another session's slot or a separate summariser model; verified by asserting the summariser request carries the assigned `id_slot`.
- **AC3 — Immediate release.** The session's local dispatch lease / slot ownership is released immediately after the summariser returns (success, failure, or timeout — and also when the boundary evaluation is skipped for lack of an assigned slot) and before the remote response is streamed; no local slot stays pinned to a session that is now being served remotely. Verified by an ordering assertion in the integration test (release precedes remote stream start) and by no leaked lease in the lease registry.
- **AC4 — Fail-open, never lossy.** Summariser failure, timeout, empty/blank summary, or an exception leaves the outgoing history byte-identical to today and still dispatches remote (existing `EmptySummary` / `remote_with_guidance` guarantees are preserved — an empty summary is never injected, turns are never silently dropped). A structured `compaction_event`-style log line records session, slot, est_before/est_after, turns summarised, duration and outcome. **No remote summariser fallback** (agreed — Appendix Q3): when boundary compaction cannot run (no assigned slot, slot unavailable, or the pinned call fails) the skip is logged at **WARNING** with a stable machine-readable reason token (`boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`) and the request proceeds remote untouched.
- **AC5 — Config gating and default-off.** The boundary compaction is controlled by its **own independent knob** (`server.remote_boundary_compaction`, default `false`; agreed — Appendix Q2) that does **not** re-enable assembly-time compaction — it ships **disabled by default** in `proxy/config.yaml`; with it disabled, request handling is unchanged (regression test asserts no summariser call and identical dispatch body). Respects the operator's 2026-09-17 decision to keep prompt-assembly compaction off (`compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`).
- **AC6 — Tests.** Unit tests cover the boundary decision (fires / does not fire by session provenance and size) and the slot pin/release wiring; an integration test drives a session that is served locally and then routed remote, asserting exactly one summarisation call, the compacted body on the wire, and the slot released.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** `docs/llama-router.md` (compaction section), the new config keys with explanatory comments in `proxy/config.yaml`, and module docstrings are updated to describe the boundary trigger, its knob, and its fail-open behaviour.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Operator kill-switch must be honoured.** Proxy-side compaction was deliberately disabled (LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6, operator request 2026-09-17) after `summarizer_failed` churn. Boundary compaction re-introduces a narrower form and must therefore be independently gated, default-off, and easy to revert.
- **Never another session's slot, never a remote summariser.** Reuse must be the session's own assigned slot only; if it has none (or the pinned call fails) boundary compaction is skipped and logged at WARNING — there is no `models.compact` / dedicated-summariser fallback in this increment (Appendix Q3).
- **No slot hold across the remote stream.** Release happens on summariser completion, not on remote response completion.
- **Latency is added before remote TTFT.** Summarisation time is charged to the request, so a timeout bound and a minimum-size guard are required to avoid compacting small sessions.
- **Local model serves the summarisation.** `id_slot` is supported by llama-server chat completions (already used by `proxy/benchmarks/slot_snapshot_benchmark.py`), but prefilling the summariser prompt overwrites that slot's KV — acceptable only because the session is leaving local.
- **No client-protocol change.** Behaviour stays inside the proxy; response headers may mirror the existing `X-Compaction-*` bridge.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — pure decision + planning (`should_compact_session`, `decide_session_compaction`, `plan_session_compaction`, `truncate_backstop`, `log_compaction_event`, churn collector). Fully tested, no live remote-boundary trigger.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — `build_local_summarizer` (posts to `http://localhost:<llama_port>/v1/chat/completions`, **no `id_slot`**) and `build_compact_summarizer` (remote `models.compact` chain Muse→DeepSeek, falling back to local).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_evaluate_session_compaction` and `evaluate_and_apply_compaction` (idempotent per request, mutates `body_json` live, marks session compacted, `#compaction_evaluated`); `_release_local_dispatch` / `_spawn_detached_release` for lease release.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — compaction evaluated inside `proxy_to_local` (`_handle_session` path) and enforced via `_route_remote_with_compaction_guidance` when the session cannot be compacted.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_evaluate_compaction_for_bypass` is called only when a **local** entry is skipped for size (~:11748). `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (remote-only chains) and `proxy_remote.py` (`proxy_to_remote`) never evaluate compaction.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_id_for_session` (assign), `_assigned_slot_for_session` (read-only lookup), `_slot_owners` registry keyed per endpoint, `SlotLockCoordinator`.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0` (0 disables; advisory + 429 gate share the knob), `compaction_dry_run: false`, `summarizer_*` keys, `models.compact` chain.
- Evidence base: `docs/session-compaction-design.md`, `docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md`, `docs/session-compaction-pi-comparison.md`.

## Desired change

Extend the existing machinery rather than duplicate it:

1. Add a **boundary decision** (new helper in `compaction.py`, e.g. `decide_boundary_compaction`) that fires only when (a) the outgoing provider is `type: remote`, (b) the session has **recorded local provenance** (at least one prior locally-served turn in the session store — not a live slot assignment), and (c) the session estimate clears a documented **minimum-size guard** (the guard is configurable, defaulted, and logged when it suppresses compaction).
2. Call it from the remote dispatch point(s) — the remote entry of `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` and the remote-only `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` / `proxy_to_remote` path, whichever the implementation finds single-channel — reusing `evaluate_and_apply_compaction` where its semantics fit.
3. Give the summariser the session's assigned slot (`id_slot`), and release the session's local dispatch lease the moment the summariser returns (or the moment the evaluation is skipped for lack of a slot).
4. Add the independent `server.remote_boundary_compaction` knob (**default `false`**, does not touch `compaction_trigger_ratio`) with validation alongside `validate_compaction_config`, and document it.
5. **No remote summariser fallback**: when the pinned local call cannot run, skip with a WARNING carrying a stable reason token; the request goes remote with its history untouched.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — Needs a boundary-decision helper (provenance + size gates) alongside `decide_session_compaction`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — Needs the boundary hook to reuse `evaluate_and_apply_compaction` and `_release_local_dispatch` ordering.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — Needs the call site in the remote dispatch cycle(s) (~:10339 `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, ~:11748 bypass block) plus config validation for `server.remote_boundary_compaction`.
- `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` — Candidate single-channel hook immediately before the remote POST in `proxy_to_remote` (~:743).
- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — Needs `id_slot` pinning on the local summariser request; the `models.compact` chain is explicitly **not** a fallback for this path (skip + WARNING instead).
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — Provides `_assigned_slot_for_session` / lease release primitives; may need a read-only "session has local provenance" accessor.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `server.remote_boundary_compaction` (default `false`) + comments in the `--- Session compaction config ---` block.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — New unit + integration tests for the trigger, slot pin, and release ordering.
- `docs/llama-router.md` — Document the boundary trigger and its knob.

## Related work

- `LP-0MTGBOOJY004OWPI` — Core summarization compaction (fast + cheap modes): the underlying planner being re-armed.
- `LP-0MU5IBXD4000POV0` / `LP-0MU5ICX7H007QKVC` — Shared `evaluate_and_apply_compaction` helper and its bypass-path wiring: the reuse surface.
- `LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6` — Disable proxy-side session compaction (operator request): why the feature is currently dark, and the constraint this item must respect.
- `LP-0MTT0O74N009E7N2` — `models.compact` (Muse → DeepSeek) summariser chain: current summariser target, the alternative to slot reuse.
- `LP-0MTXCQA8I0038J4X` — Dedicated Qwen2.5-7B summariser model: previously chosen to isolate summarisation from the main slot — directly in tension with slot reuse here.
- `LP-0MU1RXEY10075TUU` / `LP-0MTVJF5HU007ISP1` — Summariser timeout / `summarizer_failed` history: the failure mode the fail-open AC must preserve.
- `LP-0MU44KSMS002DBWA` / `LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8` — `X-Compaction-*` metadata headers: reusable observability surface for the remote response.
- `LP-0MTXEED8E003EDM8`, `LP-0MTXGU9N1009QNSB` — post-compaction session-history and durability semantics that the boundary path inherits.
- `LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4` (blocked) — `too_large` promotion strips local from the chain: the boundary case where local is never attempted, relevant to AC1's provenance definition.

## Risks and assumptions

- **R1 — Deadlock/contention on the pinned slot.** If the session's slot is still processing an abandoned earlier request, the summariser waits on it; mitigation: bounded timeout, fail-open, and `SlotLockCoordinator` ordering rather than a new lock.
- **R2 — Quality loss on the remote turn.** The remote LLM sees a summary instead of verbatim history, and (if persisted) the compacted history replaces the session's own record; mitigation: keep the existing retention invariant (system prompt + first user message verbatim), mark the summary message, and log every event.
- **R3 — Added latency before remote TTFT.** Mitigation: minimum-size guard so small sessions are never summarised; timeout default from `compaction_summarizer_timeout`.
- **R4 — Repeated compaction churn** on every local→remote bounce; mitigation: reuse the existing `CompactionChurnCollector` and the idempotent `compaction_evaluated` flag.
- **R5 — Scope creep into re-enabling assembly-time compaction or changing the summariser chain.** Record such ideas as linked work items, not scope.
- **A1 — "Work item" in the seed means the agent session** tracked by the proxy (`X-Session-Id`), not a Worklog work item.
- **A2 — "The slot assigned to the work item"** is the per-session slot in `_slot_owners` on the active local endpoint.
- **A3 — `id_slot` pinning is available on the local llama-server chat-completions endpoint** (precedent: `proxy/benchmarks/slot_snapshot_benchmark.py`).
- **A4 — Boundary compaction is a strictly narrower trigger than the disabled assembly-time compaction**, so enabling one does not imply the other.
- **A5 — Duplicate check performed:** no completed item implements local→remote boundary compaction; nearest overlaps are the planner (`LP-0MTGBOOJY004OWPI`), the reuse helper (`LP-0MU5IBXD4000POV0`) and the disable decision (`LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6`). This item is therefore scoped to the new trigger + slot reuse + release.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

Answered by the producer (operator) in this session; recorded once, idempotently.

- **Q1 — Trigger precondition.** Which definition of "started local" should gate boundary compaction?
  - (a) the session currently holds a local slot assignment in `_slot_owners` (cheapest signal);
  - (b) any remote dispatch for a session with at least one prior locally-served turn recorded in the session store;
  - (c) (a) or (b) plus a minimum estimated-token threshold.
  - **Answer (producer): (b) + size guard** — provenance is the recorded locally-served turn; a small minimum-size guard prevents summarising trivial sessions. Slot-owner state is explicitly *not* the signal, so a released or save/restored slot cannot disqualify an otherwise qualifying session. Source: interactive reply (this session). Reflected in AC1.
- **Q2 — Config gating.** New independent knob (leaving `server.compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`, i.e. assembly-time compaction, off) or fold into the existing knob (which would silently re-enable assembly-time compaction)?
  - **Answer (producer): new independent knob** — `server.remote_boundary_compaction` (default `false`). The operator's 2026-09-17 decision to keep proxy-side assembly-time compaction off (`LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6`) stands. Source: interactive reply (this session). Reflected in AC5.
- **Q3 — Behaviour when the session's slot is unavailable** (no assignment, slot busy/abandoned, or the pinned call fails): fall back to the dedicated summariser chain (`models.compact` Muse→DeepSeek, then Qwen2.5-7B) and compact anyway, or skip compaction and dispatch the untouched history remote?
  - **Answer (producer): skip, and log the skip as a warning** — fail-open with no remote summariser fallback in this increment. Source: interactive reply (this session). Reflected in AC4; a `models.compact` fallback remains an explicitly out-of-scope follow-up idea (R5).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MQ5NIONU002CACT** – Local-to-remote fallback (completed)
- **LP-0MU5I99TW000ALCO** – Regression test: compaction evaluated on bypassed sessions (completed)
- **LP-0MTV5GFL8007WSK2** – Fix compaction dry-run advisory logging suppressed by logger hierarchy (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mtt0o74n009e7n2, 0mu1rxey10075tuu, 0mvsm06lb001pru4, abandoned, ac1 (+453 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+450 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+450 more)

# Tune idle-admit eligibility to prefill feasibility (measured 0/31 conversion)

Discovered from: LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (lease-gate decision item) — the AC5
tuning follow-up for LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the idle-admission override (`server.local_idle_admit_enabled`)
to admit only requests the local backend can prefill to first byte inside
`local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / the ETA-guard queue budget, so the override
no longer spends GPU time on doomed prefills with zero served responses.

## Measured evidence (window 2026-10-22 21:48:05 → 2026-10-23 21:48:05)

31 `routing_idle_admit` events, **0 conversions** (0/31 local first bytes):

- 22 dispatched to a local slot and cancelled at `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
  (90 s deadline in force at the time; `lease_extended_during_prefill ...
  progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` → no observable prefill progress
  before the deadline), then detoured remote.
- 9 rejected on arrival by the ETA admission guard
  (`local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`,
  projected prefill 63–362 s vs the 60 s contention-queue budget).
- 0 refused by the `local_lease_active` gate; 0 first bytes.

Admitted prompt sizes 39–119 K cold tokens; window-wide `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
totalled 482 (= ~90 s per slot per abort). The after window was ~2× busier than
the before window (large_context_bypass 1,790 → 3,702; remote fallbacks 6,953 →
12,888), so this is a heavy-load measurement; the mechanism (admit → ETA-refuse
or deadline-abort) is load-independent.

Machine artifact: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`.

## Scope (candidate mechanisms to evaluate with the evidence)

- Prompt-size / projected-prefill eligibility **at admit time**: refuse the
  idle admit (keep the economic remote fallback) when `evaluate_admission`
  prices projected prefill beyond the deadline or the ETA guard would reject —
  i.e. make the override's admitted verdict consistent with the guard's
  (LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 AC3c already consults the guard; measure whether the
  dispatched-and-cancelled residue remains because the guard's calibrated
  refusal and the deadline disagree).
- Priority gating: only admit below a `high`-priority tier if interactive
  latency risk is unacceptable.
- Only if the 0-conversion persists after eligibility: reconsider the
  prefill-aware idle clock (option 5 of LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW) — the measured
  window had **zero** silent-prefill refusals, so this is the fallback, not
  the primary fix.
- Explicitly NOT in scope: preempting foreign dispatch leases — rejected in
  LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (option 1 decision); do not reopen without new evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The override's admit decision is priced against projected prefill
   feasibility (ETA-guard budget + prefill deadline) and the measured
   0/31-conversion outcome is used as the regression signal: after the change,
   an equivalent window must show idle-admitted dispatches either converting
   to a first byte or being refused **before** dispatch (no
   `prefill_deadline_exceeded` on an idle-admitted session).
2. The fix is fail-safe: it can only refuse admissions the current code
   admits — it can never admit a request the guard or deadline refuses today.
3. Any new knob is config-read at dispatch time / hot-reloadable
   (`POST /admin/reload-config`), default preserves today's behaviour until
   the tuning demonstrates improvement (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC4).
4. Unit tests cover: admit-eligibility refusal on projected prefill beyond
   the deadline; the unchanged `context_too_large` cap; a calibrated vs
   uncalibrated (fail-open) bucket; and that the lease gate is untouched.
5. Docs: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` knob
   comments and `proxy/README.md` updated; decision on the flag recorded on
   LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF (window outcome was `measure`/`tune`, not
   `enable_by_default`).

## Related work

- LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB — parent decision (option 1: lease gate unchanged).
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — parent measurement (window AC1–AC4 of record).
- LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J — ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review
  (budget/deadline re-derivation).
- LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I — residual deadline evictions with zero prefill progress.
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 / LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U — guard/deadline bounds the
  override already consults.

## Problem statement

The free-slot (direct-dispatch) admission guard in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` already records the governing decision reason verbatim for the deadline, deadline-relative safety-budget and flat cold-prefill-budget refusals (shipped with LP-0MVQ23API001UOET, commit `0466f5db`), but **no test pins that behaviour on the direct path**: the reason-contract tables drive only `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` through the free-slot route, so a regression could silently restore the 2026-10-25 retry-storm shape — a `Retry-After` advertised for a prompt that waiting cannot heal — whenever a local slot happens to be free.

## Users

- **Proxy operators / on-call engineers.** Story: *As an on-call engineer reading `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` and a client `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, I want the token to name the bound that actually refused local, so I can tell a temporal refusal (wait) from a permanent one (compact) without cross-referencing the guard's internal logic.*
- **Local-preferred clients (agents).** Story: *As an agent that is pinned local, I want a `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusal to say `retryable: false` and never hand me a `Retry-After`, so I compact my prompt instead of re-driving the same over-budget request in a retry loop.*
- **Proxy maintainers.** Story: *As a maintainer, I want both dispatch paths (queue and free-slot) covered by one table-driven contract, so adding a refusal reason cannot land with retry semantics on one path only.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Direct-path reason pass-through is table-driven and complete.** `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` drives every admission-guard reason through the **free-slot** (direct) path end-to-end via `proxy_with_fallback` — `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`, `prefill_budget_exceeded`, and the ETA/budget case — asserting both `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` and body `reason` equal the governing decision reason, with `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` used only where the free-slot ETA/budget bound itself is the cause.
2. **A free-slot over-budget request refuses without a timer.** With a free local slot and a prompt above `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, the end-to-end refusal through `proxy_with_fallback` carries `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`, no `Retry-After` header, `retryable: false`, `suggested_action` naming compaction, and the token evidence (`new_tokens` / `budget_tokens`) on both headers and body.
3. **The governing reason reaches the recorded attempt and the dispatch log.** The `local_admission_reject` attempt diagnostics and the `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback ... reason=<token>` log line name the governing reason (not `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`) for the deadline, safety-budget and cold-budget refusals; the line still carries `free_slot=true`.
4. **Regression guard on the label.** A test fails if `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` is (re)emitted as the refusal reason for any non-ETA-budget decision reason, on either path.
5. **Docs verified/updated.** `proxy/docs/routing.md` (the "Local-only is enforced on every exit" exit table and the reason→retry-timing table) states that only the free-slot ETA/budget reason keeps the `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` token; any wording change lands with the code comments.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Test-first, behaviour-preserving.** The mapping in `provider.py` (lines ~11938–11955) is believed correct; the deliverable is the pinning test set. If a test disproves the belief, fix the production code — do **not** weaken the test.
- **The client token vocabulary must not change for existing cases.** `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` stays the free-slot ETA/budget refusal token; it is pinned as a documented exit token by `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py` and the refusal-routing docs.
- **Do not disturb the too-large pin-decline contract** (LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 AC4): a pin-local client with a `prefill_budget_exceeded` / `context_too_large` verdict is promoted to the remote tiers rather than refused, so the free-slot over-budget *refusal* shape is observable on the exhaustion path (no fallback provider) — assert both shapes if both are reachable from the free-slot path.
- **No timing-contract changes.** `_refusal_retry_timing` / `NOT_TIME_RETRYABLE_REFUSAL_REASONS` (`provider.py` ~4498–4530) are the single source of retry semantics; assert through them, do not re-implement their arithmetic.
- No ad-hoc full-suite runs: use the test skill (`/skill:test`).

## Existing state

## Desired change

Add free-slot rows to the reason-contract tables so each admission-guard reason is forced through the direct path, plus one end-to-end free-slot over-budget refusal test proving the no-timer/`retryable: false`/token-evidence contract; replace the inline label re-derivation in `test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` with a call through `_prefill_admission_guard` (or leave it and cover the gap in the contract table — implementer's call, documented in the commit).

- LP-0MVQ23API001UOET — "Refactor: reason-aware timing decision for refusal paths": landed the `_direct_reason` pass-through in commit `0466f5db`

# Feature — Enforce the post-deadline thrash gate at every local-dispatch entry; terminal in-request detour

Child of LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV. Implementation slice: after the deterministic tests
(C1) pin the mechanism, make the cancelled session's claim on the local gate end with
the cancellation — the thrash-cooldown gate engages for EVERY local dispatch attempt
(including paths that bypass provider.py's chain gate), the same request does not
re-dispatch local after the deadline detour, and any remaining lease is bounded
≤300 s.

## Target outcome

A local dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` stops holding the local
dispatch gate: no in-request local re-dispatch acquiring a fresh lease ~150 ms after
the release; the per-session thrash cooldown demonstrably engages at every local
dispatch entry; `local_prefill_in_flight` never outlives the dispatch it marks; every
remaining hold is bounded ≤300 s (parent AC1-AC3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1. Every path that can acquire a local dispatch lease consults the per-session
  thrash cooldown before acquisition — including direct local paths that bypass
  provider.py's chain gate (the shape C1's isolation test surfaced). A session whose
  cooldown is armed is refused (`routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`)
  with the chain falling to the next provider. C1's gate-engagement test goes green.
  Rollback knob `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 0` still disables the gate.
- AC2. The deadline detour is terminal for local within that request: a request-scoped
  marker set on `prefill_deadline_exceeded` prevents the same request from acquiring a
  fresh lease after release (the ~150 ms post-release fresh lease is impossible). C1's
  re-dispatch test goes green.
- AC3. After the cancellation the lease, `local_prefill_in_flight` marker are cleared
  BEFORE any retry, and the cancelled upstream prefill stream is closed (proven dead)
  so `_extend_prefill_lease` cannot re-extend from a stale marker (no
  `lease_extended_during_prefill ... in_flight=True` after release). C1's marker test
  goes green.
- AC4. Any remaining hold is bounded ≤300 s from its last progress for every
  acquisition path (deadline detour, same-session re-acquisition, active-expired
  sweep) without weakening the 180 s no-progress watchdog or the 10 s sweep cadence.
  C1's bound test goes green.
- AC5. Legitimate long prefills are unaffected: a live, progressing prefill keeps its
  lease (no-preemption same-session semantics preserved); first-byte latency stays
  inside `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`; a successful local first byte clears
  the cooldown per the recovery-fraction rule (parent constraints).
- AC6. Changed-scope test gate passes and the full suite stays green with the fix.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken: the prefill deadline (120 s) detour-not-kill backstop, the
  no-progress watchdog (180 s), the 10 s sweep, the thrash cooldown (600 s / rollback
  knob 0), no-preemption same-session lease re-acquisition for genuine in-flight
  prefills.
- Scope: do NOT absorb lease-fairness renewal caps (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0) — record any
  overlap as related work, keep that item's scope there.
- Fix the mechanism C1 identifies (bypass and/or arm-key mismatch); a renewal cap alone
  is insufficient if the gate remains unengaged (parent AC1 mandates an engaged gate).

## Risky assumptions

- The incident re-dispatch is a same-request/retry client pattern (pi/opencode retries
  on 503); the request-scoped marker must not block unrelated concurrent requests from
  the same session (the session cooldown covers those).
- Closing the upstream prefill stream is sufficient to prevent stale-marker
  re-extension (verify with C1's marker test).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a request-scoped post-deadline marker set in the `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
   path and checked at the lease-acquisition choke point; local is terminal for that
   request (chain falls to the next provider).
2. Consult the thrash cooldown at the single choke point every local dispatch passes
   (router.py `proxy_to_local` immediately before `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`) so
   direct bypass paths engage; keep the existing provider.py gate.
3. Harden the release path (deadline + measured-abort twins) so record + marker
   removal and upstream-stream close (bounded by `disconnect_cleanup_timeout`) complete
   before any retry can observe stale state.
4. Update code comments at the changed sites; keep the existing log vocabulary
   (`routing_skip_local`, `lease_released`, `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started`).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`proxy_to_local`, `prefill_deadline_exceeded` block)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_*`, `_extend_lease_during_prefill`)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (local branch + any direct dispatch paths C1 surfaces)
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` (harness extended by C1)
- Related: `proxy/proxy/ui.py` (`_dispatch_local_model_load` direct
  `srv.proxy_to_local`), per C1's cause comment

# Load-normalise the AC3 denial check in the idle-admit measurement

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the AC3 `local_dispatch_denied` check normalised to
window load (per bypass/fallback event), so the measured `+9.3 %` per-hour
denial "increase" (window 2026-10-22 21:48 → 2026-10-23 21:48, ~2× busier than
the before window) is judged on a load-independent signal instead of a
confounded raw rate.

## Measured evidence (artifact `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `local_dispatch_denied` raw | 66.0 /h | 72.1 /h | **+9.3 %** (> 5 % band → fail) |
| `large_context_bypass` events | 1,790 | 3,702 | +107 % |
| Remote fallback events | 6,953 | 12,888 | +85 % |
| Denials per bypass+fallback event | 1,584/8,743 = 0.181 | 1,731/16,590 = 0.104 | −42 % |

The raw rate cannot distinguish "the override causes more denials" from "a 2×
heavier window produces proportionally more denials". The tool currently
implements only the raw per-hour rate (`scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`:
`denied_before_rate`/`denied_after_rate`, `_DENIED_TOLERANCE_PCT = 5.0`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` reports a load-normalised denial rate — denials per bypass+fallback event — alongside the existing per-hour rate, in both the AC3 check and the JSON/markdown output.
- The AC3 verdict uses the normalised rate for pass/fail (the raw per-hour rate remains reported), so a raw increase caused purely by higher load no longer fails the check; a genuine per-event increase still fails.
- Tests cover: the normalised-rate arithmetic against the exact window numbers above (fail → pass), a synthetic per-event denial increase that still fails the check, and backward compatibility of all existing JSON keys and exit codes.
- Re-running the tool `--window-closed` on the closed window records the AC3 verdict on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD next to the baselines table, with the normalised numbers and sample counts.
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` documents the normalised metric definition and why the raw per-hour rate is load-confounded.

## Key Files

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`

# Intake brief: join hard-wrapped AC bullets in tree_coverage extraction

## Goal (user story)

As a planner/auditor agent — or the producer reading its coverage report — I want `extract_acceptance_criteria()` to return a hard-wrapped AC bullet as one complete sentence, so the parent↔child AC coverage review compares whole requirements instead of truncated fragments and stops producing a false `stop` / 0 % coverage verdict on well-maintained, wrapped items.

## Problem statement

`extract_acceptance_criteria()` treats every physical line of an `## Acceptance Criteria` section as a separate AC, so a bullet hard-wrapped at ~80 columns is cut at its first line. Both sides of the parent↔child comparison are truncated the same way, parent↔child Jaccard scores collapse to 0.05–0.18 (below the 0.2 auto-close floor), and `run_coverage_review()` answers `recommendation: "stop"` with 0 % coverage for items whose children demonstrably cover the scope.

## Users

- **Planner and intake agents (downtime-dispatched, no interactive approver).** As a planner agent, I want the AC coverage helper to read whole ACs, so a wrapped item is not held at `intake_complete`/`plan_complete` by a parsing artefact and I do not have to override the helper with a hand-built per-AC table.
- **Producer / operator reviewing stage advancement.** As the producer, I want a `stop` recommendation to mean a real coverage gap, so I can trust the gate instead of re-verifying every wrapped item by hand.
- **Auditors.** As the audit skill, I want the coverage evidence to reflect requirement text, so coverage percentages and gap-conflict messages are meaningful.

## Acceptance criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria()` returns one AC entry per top-level bullet, joining the bullet's wrapped continuation lines into that entry: a bullet spanning N physical lines yields exactly one string containing the full sentence, with intra-entry whitespace collapsed to single spaces.
- Continuation joining inserts a single space between wrapped lines except where the previous line ends with a hyphen attached to the preceding word (`high-` + `priority`, `per-` + `request`), which is rejoined without a space; a hyphen preceded by whitespace keeps the space.
- Existing extraction semantics are preserved unchanged: deeper-indented sub-list markers are still excluded as ACs and their text is not appended to the parent AC; a blank line ends the current AC entry (an unmarked prose paragraph after a blank line is not merged into it); lines inside a fenced code block and table rows are not appended; unwrapped single-line bullets and ordered items (`1.`, `1)`) extract exactly as they do today.
- Scope and invariants preserved: `compute_coverage()`, `jaccard_similarity()`, `resolve_coverage_gaps()`, the 0.4 coverage threshold and the 0.2 auto-close floor are unchanged, and the fail-closed path in `run_coverage_review()` still returns `recommendation: "stop"` with the existing warning when an AC section yields no parseable entry (existing fail-closed tests pass unmodified).
- Regression tests cover, at minimum: one hard-wrapped multi-line bullet yielding one complete AC; mixed wrapped and unwrapped bullets plus a wrapped ordered item; a wrapped bullet that contains a nested sub-list (sub-list excluded, parent text complete); a hyphen-broken word rejoined without a space; a blank-line-terminated entry not over-merged; and the untouched existing `TestExtractAcceptanceCriteria` cases.
- Re-running `run_coverage_review()` on `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD` after the fix records a before/after per-AC best-match score table in a comment on this item, showing the score movement (pre-fix 0.053–0.182 measured during intake; expected post-fix 0.115–0.389) with at least two of the five parent ACs clearing the 0.2 auto-close floor, so the review no longer resolves zero of five gaps.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change: the `extract_acceptance_criteria()` docstring states the continuation-join and hyphen rules, and any doc that describes per-line AC semantics is corrected (no `docs/` page currently documents extraction; `skill/intake/SKILL.md` and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` reference only `apply_coverage_review`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` included; run through `/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- The change is extraction-only: `compute_coverage()`, `jaccard_similarity()`, `resolve_coverage_gaps()`, the 0.4 coverage threshold and the 0.2 auto-close floor are untouched. Threshold or tokenisation tuning is a separate item if the post-fix signal is still too weak.
- Fail-closed behaviour is preserved: an AC section that yields no parseable entry still returns `recommendation: "stop"` with the existing warning message.
- The fix lands in the framework repo `SorraAgents` (`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`), while this work item lives in the `llm` worklog — the implementing commit hash must be recorded in a comment here, and the implement phase must work in the SorraAgents checkout, not beneath `~/projects/llm`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill`, so edits take effect immediately for every agent; the change must therefore be correct and tested in one pass (no partial behaviour left live).
- Unit tests must remain hermetic — fixtures inline in the test module, no `wl` subprocess and no dependency on another project's live worklog store for CI.
- Scope-creep guard: re-working the coverage report format, semantic matching, or stop-word handling is explicitly out of scope.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (1,092 lines): `extract_acceptance_criteria()` scans the AC section line by line, strips `- ` / `+ ` / `N.` / `N)` markers via `_strip_ac_list_marker()`, and appends each marker line as one AC; non-marker lines are ignored entirely (function at line 374). Nested-indent exclusion was added in `7b1aeece` (SA-0MVO7R2WU0058RNJ), which also added the fail-closed path.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — `TestExtractAcceptanceCriteria` holds the 20 existing extraction cases (nested bullet vs numbered, indented section, multi-digit numbering, bold-led items, document order). No wrapped-bullet case exists.
- Consumers: `run_coverage_review()` / `apply_coverage_review()` are called by the intake and plan skills; no other module imports the extractor.
- Measured on `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD` (5 wrapped parent ACs, 3 children) during this intake, with a prototype that joins continuation lines:

| Parent AC | Best match now | Best match with join | 0.2 auto-close floor |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| AC1 (≥24 h window numbers) | 0.182 | 0.250 | cleared |
| AC2 (idle-admitted percentiles) | 0.077 | 0.115 | still below |
| AC3 (denials / timeouts) | 0.056 | 0.118 | still below |
| AC4 (interactive tier) | 0.053 | 0.152 | still below |
| AC5 (enable / tuning decision) | 0.158 | 0.389 | cleared |

  The prototype also reproduced the join hazard behind the hyphen rule: `high-
priority` joined with a space yields `high- priority`.
- The pre-fix review of that item resolved 0 of 5 gaps (`recommendation: "stop"`, `coverage_pct: 0.0`, best-match scores 0.05–0.18) and had to be overridden manually with an evidence table (comment `LP-C0MVSB1GR6007O3EN`).

## Desired change

Accumulate continuation lines into the open AC entry instead of discarding them: when a line inside the AC section carries no list marker, is not blank, is not a heading, and is not inside a fenced code block, append it to the current AC with the join rule above (single space, or no space after a word-attached hyphen) and normalise whitespace. Flush the accumulated entry on the next top-level marker, a blank line, or the end of the section. Nested markers keep their current "ignored, not promoted, not appended" behaviour. Update the docstring to state these rules.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `extract_acceptance_criteria()` and `_strip_ac_list_marker()`; continuation accumulation plus docstring (SorraAgents repo)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — new wrapped-bullet regression cases in `TestExtractAcceptanceCriteria`
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — only if the coverage-review description needs a note (currently delegates to `apply_coverage_review`)
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — same, verify no per-line semantics are described

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — blank line terminates an entry.** Hard-wrapped bullets are contiguous in practice; treating a blank line as an entry boundary keeps stray prose out of ACs and matches the "wrapped bullet" root cause. Consequence: a bullet with an intentional blank line inside it is read as two fragments of one AC.
- **Assumption — hyphen rule is `word-` immediately followed by the continuation**, i.e. no whitespace before the hyphen. `text -` (spaced dash) keeps the separating space.
- **Assumption — "no longer reports all 5 as uncovered"** is measured as score movement plus resolved-gap count (2 of 5 at the 0.2 floor), not as `coverage_pct` at the 0.4 threshold. With the fix alone `coverage_pct` stays 0 % for that item because AC2–AC4 remain below 0.4; reaching `proceed` needs scoring work that is out of scope.
- **Risk — over-merging.** A prose paragraph or note between bullets could be appended to the previous AC; mitigated by the blank-line/heading/fence boundaries and by a dedicated regression test.
- **Risk — silent behaviour change for consumers.** Intake and plan both gate on this helper, so a malformed join would wrongly advance or block stages; mitigated by keeping the full existing test class green and adding the mixed/nested cases.
- **Risk — cross-repo traceability.** The item is tracked in `llm` but the code is in `SorraAgents`; a missing commit reference would make the fix unauditable.
- **Scope-creep risk:** better coverage discrimination (stop words, thresholds, semantic similarity) is tempting once the numbers are visible — record it as a linked follow-up item, not in this change.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD` — Measure idle-aware local admission impact over ≥24h (before/after): the item whose coverage review produced the false `stop`; it is now `plan_complete` with manual per-AC evidence.
- `LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF`, `LP-0MVRCLPVI0057116`, `LP-0MVSAZLNL007B072` — the children used as the child-side corpus for the measurement above.
- `SA-0MVO7R2WU0058RNJ` (commit `7b1aeece`, SorraAgents) — previous change to the same function: nested-bullet AC promotion fix plus fail-closed on an unparseable AC section; established the test class and the indentation semantics preserved here.
- `LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E` — notes the same function in its planning context (numbered-AC extraction), showing this helper is a recurring source of false coverage signals.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer answers were obtained in this session (downtime dispatch, no interactive approver). The seed context was sufficient to draft the brief; the entries below record the interpretations the brief proceeds on.

- **OPEN QUESTION 1** (directed to the producer/operator; matters because it decides whether AC3 of this item is met by extraction alone): Does "no longer reports all 5 parent ACs as uncovered" mean the *resolved-gap* signal must move (scores above the 0.2 auto-close floor, `coverage_pct` at 0.4 unchanged), or must the 0.4-scored `coverage_pct` itself rise above 0 %?
  - **Assumption used:** the resolved-gap signal — the item's own parenthetical says "score movement is what matters, not a specific threshold", and raising the 0.4-threshold coverage would require scoring changes the root-cause analysis does not describe.
- **Q: Where does the extractor live and which tests cover it?** — Answer (research, no producer input needed): `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` in the framework repo `SorraAgents` (the item's `skills/...` path is the same tree, renamed `skill/`), with `TestExtractAcceptanceCriteria` in `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — not `skill/plan/tests/` as the item's Key Files suggested. Evidence: `grep -rn extract_acceptance_criteria skill/`, `git log -- skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`.
- **Q: Do wrapped ACs really explain the 0 % coverage, or is scoring also at fault?** — Answer (research): both sides are truncated, and joining both sides lifts best-match scores from 0.053–0.182 to 0.115–0.389 (table above), i.e. extraction is the primary defect; AC2–AC4 stay below the 0.4 threshold, which is scoring/tokenisation territory and out of scope. Evidence: prototype extraction run over `wl show` output for `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD` and its three children.
- **Q: Is editing this agent-infrastructure file authorised?** — Answer (interpretation): yes for this item — it exists as a producer-filed bug with explicit ACs naming the function, so the item is the authorisation; any behaviour beyond continuation joining (thresholds, scoring) still needs its own item. Recorded so the producer can correct the reading at review.

Full untruncated automated report sidecar: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF7KSJW007L2QF** – End-to-end integration test and regression gate (completed)
- **LP-0MVF7KO8C005NB59** – Quota hard stop and cost guard (completed)
- **LP-0MRGUJ3QR002K18G** – Release local model slot immediately when session is routed to remote fallback (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, acs, agent, already, also (+99 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: acceptance, acs, agent, already, also (+99 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, acs, agent, already, also (+99 more)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-29T05:03Z (plan, session `herdr-1793250095-1441524-3433`) — auto-plan path (`plan-if-needed` → `skip`, Effort Small / Risk Low): no child decomposition created; six automated review stages run against the existing content. Requirements & AC alignment review added one AC ("Scope and invariants preserved") promoting two existing Constraints (extraction-only change; fail-closed behaviour preserved) into testable criteria. Key Files block validated syntactically (`validate_key_files_format()` → no issues) and all four paths confirmed present in the `SorraAgents` checkout. Pre-fix measurement in the Existing state table re-verified against the live worklog (best-match scores 0.182 / 0.077 / 0.056 / 0.053 / 0.158 on `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD`; parent ACs currently extract as 7–12-word truncated fragments), so the AC5 evidence requirement is achievable. No other content changes.
